Two years ago, Sonos expanded from the wireless speaker market into the over-ear headphone space. Now, Sonos appears ready to launch a new-generation successor positioned higher and equipped with artificial intelligence technology.

Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones are about to debut

Chris Welch reported for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra, an upgraded successor to the 2024 Ace headphones.

An application document disclosed by the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on Monday mentioned the product name and showed up to five colour options, more than the original model's two colours of black and white.

Sonos plans to hold a product launch event in September. According to the document's timeline, the Ace Ultra is likely one of the products to appear that day.

The document also contains technical clues, indicating the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

Bloomberg reported that CEO Tom Conrad admitted that the original headphones lacked sufficient whole-home integration capabilities when launched, failing to establish a clear differentiation in the fiercely competitive market for similar products.

This time, Sonos appears determined to integrate its hardware more directly into a broader artificial intelligence strategy.

Conrad positioned the company's growth opportunity in conversational computing and predictive intelligence for the home environment, positioning Sonos devices as hardware capable of operating across rooms and mastering home lifestyle patterns.

The company has expanded Sonos Voice Control to support Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 launched in March, equipped with an H2 chip, stronger noise cancellation, and real-time translation capabilities. Siri artificial intelligence will extend to AirPods via iOS 27.

For details on the upcoming Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones, please refer to the full Bloomberg report.
